correctness.rationale: For every integer index at least two, the proof exhausts all relations on the distinguished elements in the ternary group language and reduces a two-round game to eight pointed rank-one types. Each type has an explicit order and square-root criterion derived from the dicyclic presentation and the congruence \(2j\equiv k\pmod{2n}\). Exact checks agree for all group elements at indices 2 through 18, all four-bit patterns at indices 2 through 40, and all class signatures through index 100. The computations support, but do not replace, the all-index argument. The sharp largest representative order is \(4\cdot12=48\).

value.rationale: This exact complete logical classification concerns all nontrivial finite dicyclic groups, a canonical nonsplit family adjoining an order-four square root of its central involution. It identifies a sharp local logical stabilization law, three genuine small exceptions, two independent arithmetic obstructions after stabilization, and an optimal 48-element representative. The eight-profile algebraic mechanism explains rather than merely tabulates the distinction; the exact fact is a useful benchmark for finite-group descriptive complexity.
